fieldMarks: Drake: glossy green head, yellow bill, white neck ring, chestnut breast, gray body and curled black tail feathers.
Hen: mottled brown with an orange bill marked with black, and orange legs.
Both sexes show a blue to purplish-blue speculum bordered in white.
behavior: Dabbles, up-ends with tail vertical, occasionally dives, and grazes on land.
Eats mostly plant material (seeds, roots, pondweeds, acorns, grain) plus insects, crustaceans and mollusks.
Hen gives the familiar loud quack; drake gives softer, reedy calls.
Readily attracted by decoys; pairs form in fall and winter.
habitat: Marshes, prairie potholes and reed-ringed sloughs, ponds, rivers, lakes, bays, grain fields and city parks; prefers fresh water.
range: Across Alaska, Canada (most numerous in the Prairie Provinces, expanding eastward) and most of the US; winters in southern Ontario and British Columbia and farther south. Also native to Europe and Asia.
